title: One MODIS pixel opened into its 10 m cells (pixel_anatomy 1.0.0)
description:
Precomputed result of recipe pixel_anatomy 1.0.0 for MODIS pixel h17v05r4005c2178 of Ait Bouguemez valley catchment (bundle row 51, column 58, centre 31.655208 N, 6.416024 W): 537 cells of 10 m, tree cover 215 cells (40.0%), grassland 254 cells (47.3%), cropland 32 cells (6.0%), bare or sparse vegetation 36 cells (6.7%). Class spectra from S2B_29SQR_20250611_0_L2A (2025-06-11); the pixel's measured NDVI on that day is 0.4766, a linear mix of the class medians (modelled) gives 0.4450; its own March to June greenness over 26 seasons has a Theil-Sen slope of +0.0570 NDVI per decade (95% interval +0.0374 to +0.0845). The pixel is an illustration chosen by judgment (rank 3 of 391 candidates), not a sample.

One pixel is an illustration, not a sample: it was chosen by judgment among the candidates of a rule (the selection record gives their number and its rank), and it says nothing about other pixels. The class spectra come from one clear day, the cells of each class inside this pixel, and one 2021 land cover map. They are not typical spectra of the classes, and a 10 m cell at the edge of a class mixes surfaces. The mix model assumes the pixel's reflectance is the share-weighted sum of its class medians. It ignores shadow, slope and variation inside a class, so its NDVI is modelled, not measured, and it differs from the measured pixel NDVI by the amount stored. NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), and on the valley floor tree cover may include orchards (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10). The 26-season series is the pixel's own March to June greenness, not adjusted for rainfall. Its trend is a descriptive Theil-Sen slope with Sen's 95% interval, and no p-value or false discovery rate class is stored for one pixel (SCI-52). Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA), so later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground. The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.

siterra:geo_selection.area_method: Count of 10 m analysis pixels whose centres fall inside the frozen polygon, EPSG:32629

operation_order: Pixel: a MODIS tile pixel named by its tile, row and column (h17v05, row 4005, column 2178); its position in the pixel trend bundle's native grid follows from the sinusoidal tile lattice; its footprint is the pixel's square in the MODIS sinusoidal grid (231.66 m), which is a four-sided shape in EPSG:32629

Cells: the 10 m cells of the strata's EPSG:32629 analysis grid whose centres lie inside the frozen polygon and, transformed to the sinusoidal grid, inside the footprint (the cell to pixel rule of place_config.cell_pixel_index). The display window is the bounding box of those cells plus 1 cell on every side, widened so that its edges lie on 20 m

Per cell: the ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 class; the Sentinel-2 monthly median NDVI and the count of dates behind it for the configured month; the true colour of the shared display composite (display only, never used in a number); whether the cell is inside the footprint and the polygon

Scene: among the Earth Search items cached for the pixel's Sentinel-2 tile and the configured month, those on the configured relative orbit with data over every footprint cell; the one with the largest share of footprint cells whose scene classification (SCL) is 4 or 5, ties by the latest date. Every candidate's share is stored

Extracts: for that scene, the windows of B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B8A, B11, B12 and SCL that cover the display window (10 m bands at 10 m; 20 m bands and SCL at 20 m), as read (uint16 digital numbers, uint8 SCL), each with its source address, COG window and sha256

Spectra: reflectance = DN / 10000 with no offset; the 20 m bands and SCL repeated 2 x 2 onto the 10 m cells; a footprint cell is kept when its SCL is 4 or 5 and every band's DN is above 0. Per WorldCover class of the footprint: the median, 25th and 75th percentile of the kept cells' reflectance in each band and the number of kept cells. The pixel's measured values: the mean reflectance of all kept cells in each band, the NDVI of the mean red (B04) and near-infrared (B08), and the median and mean of the cell NDVI

Mix model (modelled, not measured): the share of class k is s_k = footprint cells of class k / footprint cells; the mixed reflectance in band b is R(b) = sum over k of s_k times the class median M_k(b); modelled NDVI = (R(B08) - R(B04)) / (R(B08) + R(B04)). Stored with the difference from the measured pixel NDVI, and with the same formula for a reference shift of 20 percentage points of the footprint from grassland to tree cover (an example of the control, not an observation)

Series: the pixel's season greenness G(p, y) for March to June of each year 2000 to 2025, recomputed from the MOD13Q1 windows with the registered functions of pixel_trend_long_record (pixel reliability 0 and 1 kept, at least half of the 16-day periods kept, values to 5 decimals), and its Theil-Sen slope per decade with Sen's 95% interval; the builder stops unless slope and interval equal the pixel trend bundle's table at 5 decimals

Selection record: the pixels that meet the specimen's rule (Sen interval entirely above zero in March to June, every footprint cell inside the catchment, tree cover plus cropland 0.25 to 0.60 of the cells, grassland plus shrubland plus bare or sparse at least 0.35, built-up at most 0.05, at least half of the cells on sloping ground), ranked by the lower bound of the interval; stored with their number, the top five and the pixel's rank

Acceptance checks, all stored with the bundle: the cell to pixel rule reproduces the table's analysis_cells for every one of the pixels and the footprint count of this pixel; every extract's sha256 equals its record; the extracts cover the display window; no kept cell has red or near-infrared reflectance above 1.0; class cell counts add up to the footprint; the series reproduces the table; the scene is the one the scene rule gives; two runs give identical files apart from the computed time

siterra:checks.name: recompute_sample_period
siterra:checks.detail: Recomputed from the shipped extracts, the pixel trend table and the MOD13Q1 windows. The cell to pixel rule gives the table's analysis_cells for 8094 of 8094 pixels (0 differ); this pixel's footprint holds 537 cells, 537 of them inside the catchment, against 537 in the table. 11 of 11 extracts have the recorded sha256 (mismatching: none) and every window covers the 28 x 28 display window (True). 0 kept cells have red or near-infrared reflectance above 1.0; class cell counts add up to 537 of 537. The pixel's 26-season March to June series gives slope +0.05702 and interval +0.03741 to +0.08451 NDVI per decade, equal to the table's +0.05702 and +0.03741 to +0.08451 at 5 decimals (True). The scene rule applied to the stored candidates gives S2B_29SQR_20250611_0_L2A (True). The candidate rule gives 391 pixels and ranks this one 3. The whole computation run twice in one process gives identical results: True.

siterra:checks.name: units_and_scale
siterra:checks.detail: Reflectance is DN / 10000 with no offset (observation-preprocessing.md, offset rule); extracts hold the stored uint16 DN and uint8 SCL; NDVI is (near-infrared - red) / (near-infrared + red) from B08 and B04; series NDVI is the MOD13Q1 DN / 10000 season mean; slopes are NDVI per decade (1/(10 a)); coordinates are EPSG:32629 metres for the grid and decimal degrees for the footprint corners; the MODIS pixel is 231.66 m on a side.

siterra:checks.name: nodata_not_zero
siterra:checks.detail: DN 0 means no data in the extracts and occurs in 0 cells of all 11 windows; SCL 0 (no data) occurs in 0 footprint cells. A season whose half of 16-day periods are not kept has no value (null), never 0; 0 of 26 seasons are missing.

siterra:checks.name: qa_join_coverage
siterra:checks.detail: Scene classification joins every footprint cell to its bands: {'4': 286, '5': 251} cells by SCL class in the footprint (537 cells); the share with SCL 4 or 5 is 1.0. The scene rule compared 8 scenes on R094; every candidate's share is in scene-record.json.

siterra:checks.name: period_alignment
siterra:checks.detail: The scene (2025-06-11) lies in 2025-06, the month of the NDVI median and count shown for each cell, and inside the March to June window of the last season of the series.

siterra:checks.name: attribution_present
siterra:checks.detail: The Sentinel-2 notice for 2025, the MOD13Q1 v6.1 citation with DOI, subset and access date, the ESA WorldCover attribution and the Copernicus DEM notices are in siterra:attribution.

siterra:checks.name: visual_inspection_sample
siterra:checks.detail: Rendered the 28 x 28 cell window, the class spectra and the series (science/pipeline/render-pixel-anatomy.py) and inspected the image on 2026-10-29 (science lane). The footprint is a slightly turned square of 537 cells: tree cover fills its northern half, grassland its southern half, cropland lies in patches towards the north-east, and a strip of bare or sparse ground runs along its south-western edge. June NDVI is high over the tree cover and low over the grassland, and the display true colour shows the same split, dark green above and pale ground below. In the spectra, tree cover and cropland rise steeply from red to near-infrared while grassland and bare ground stay nearly flat, with the pixel mean between them, and the model value sits just below the measured value. The series swings from year to year, 2001 is its lowest season, and the straight line through it slopes upward.
